notes.title: Update 004: Track Switching
notes.notes:
Update 004 Topics

Track Switching (long winded)

Auto Testing



Track Switching 🔀

One cool aspect of developing Railborn is the unique design challenges we come across. One of these seemed trivial at first, but became more complicated as we started to conjure up the answer: how does the player switch tracks?

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45652029/b1b3a5a700d230ace9e4ad09d1ada7ae01bcdfe6.jpg"]

A couple of challenges:

Life would be simpler if Railborn’s train had a “front” – like Zelda Spirit Tracks. But – since we allow piece by piece building of your train, you decide what is the “front”, not us! Therefore, when we present the player “left” or “right” what is this all relative to?

UI! How do we present the player the UI to switch tracks? Again, most games would probably pop up an interactive menu – but again, we want players to have the ability to build their train's controlling components piece by piece in the location they choose. Making your own cockpit is cool.

 

So how do we do this? Track Switcher

The Track Switcher is a built item that has a digital display. The player can switch it to go left, straight or right. The display will always show the upcoming intersection path options.

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45652029/c5f90cddfa5b6402d78abd1b7946fb296e69429e.gif"]



How do we tell you what is the next intersection? Alright – we’re trying out an in-world icon that displays the distance and path choices so you have an idea of what’s coming up. In the example below you can see next intersection is in 48 meters, and one can go left or straight. 

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45652029/018d067f19bb75eb21f41dc7139b6767446a5b6c.gif"]

 

Switching in action 

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45652029/d2a0263c90d47ebedfa636e809bfdafad0784033.gif"]

 

Let’s get weird. So here, you can see the train changing what it considers “front” depending on the direction of travel.

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45652029/0b73fb9eaa0ec038d98ce518cf2103a5beb82a68.gif"]

 

So, what happens when your Track Switcher is facing the opposite direction of what your train thinks is front (again remember, front changes with direction of travel). Well – the display on the Track Switcher will always display the upcoming intersection in the direction of travel.

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45652029/23da808172ced4223258baea7cc8179b17a1f2c9.gif"]



Let’s see this in action:

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45652029/d4c1ef77c61b0e0bc287b5b92f5f7b4b62bbb486.gif"]

 

If that seems a bit too tricky for you – we have an easy solution (which I use) – it is to build another Track Switcher facing the other direction! All your track switchers synchronize direction, so now deciding which way to go is much simpler. Check it out:

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45652029/b9bce6213075b23ad3c3ff1c3dc605058367aa99.gif"]

 

This is what we have in mind, although once your, the Early Access brave souls get your hands on Railborn, might change.

 

 

Auto Testing 🧪

Well, this wouldn’t be an update post if there wasn’t a boring technical part. We have set up a slick little system that builds the Railborn after every check-in to our repository. We then automatically load up Railborn on our trusty old laptop equipped with a 1660 Ti - our minimum spec target. 



The test performs a few in-game operations then spits back the performance with respect to FPS, Draw calls, GPU usage, along with a few other nifty benchmarks (below). This is really handy because it lets us know which new addition to the game caused a performance hitch. It easily can be that performance suffers from a feature or addition you had no idea would be a problem. Anyway, here is a chart of our last 20 check-ins. 😊

Note cells that turn red are over our threshold for our minimum spec target and that build should be investigated.



[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45652029/27a625e2a7857a1e5acd0315531df7ff5081d7be.png"]

 

As always, please shoot out our game link to some friends for a Wishlist or two 😊 



Smashlore & Taky

notes.title: Update #002: Rooftop Runs
notes.notes:
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45652029/5a814ea68f961f9f999f6ea29da1590b9846758b.jpg"]

Well – I’m going to come right out and say it – the last month has been fantastic for the future of Railborn. Since we announced just a little while ago we have had a huge amount of interest from players like you – which means others share our vision! This is 1) motivating 2) exciting 3) tells us people want the type of game we want. Reception outside of Steam has also been mega positive! 

 

If you are new with Washbear – every official update I choose a select few topics to discuss. We have been working on so much – but for the sake of all our time, I pick just a couple of thoughts.

 
Update 002 Topics
Wishlists

VRAM

Rooftop Running

 
Wishlists🎊
How is this even a topic? Well it is! I’d provide you with an actual Wishlist update but the Steam backend seems to be having a hiccup, so I’ll save that for later this week. Needless to say you all have been AMAZING. I can’t stress enough how Wishlists contribute to the success of Railborn. So if you have a moment, please pass on the Railborn store page to your friend groups for a Wishlist. Alright, enough begging for Wishlists. 😊

 

[dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/app/2340970/Railborn/"][/dynamiclink]
VRAM 🐏
As a Steam user, I mostly enjoy updates that feature cool graphics or new mechanics. Truthfully though from the dev side – we often have a lot of “difficult to show off” work to do that is REALLY important. Our target for Railborn is to run smoothly at a High graphic setting with 4 GB video RAM. We decided on this target by looking at the Steam survey

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45652029/4ca1e2ec47b982ecf73dce6ee1359655eeb715b3.png"]

This means going deep into how we texture the world of Railborn to find efficiencies. Is there a lot of whiteboard madness tracking where every precious VRAM GB goes? Yes – there is. We come from a console background of game development so we like to statically allocate all of our textures and stream in only what we have to. This makes the game much smoother and minimize hitches.

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45652029/c795319b7f4922304b3a58b93ae270ebae5bb4c6.jpg"]

 
Roof Running 👟
In Railborn you can expand your home by unlocking and building additional train cars. Each train car can have a different style (dictated by you) and purpose (again, decided by you). Moving between train cars can be done via doors – or – my favorite – running across the roofs. When we had started making Railborn I knew this was a feature we had to have! To be clear, this was difficult from a technical point of view (I’ll save this for another post). Here is an extended version of running rooftops.

 

 [img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45652029/46adbf7593169b4b92b3ca6252d577b777f3f66e.gif"] 

The key is ensuring you build parts of your train cart roofs that are flat, and have a little point to enable you land on the next train car. I can’t wait to see all the ideas you folks come up with!

 

 

That’s it for now. Be safe our there friends! (and remember to grab us some Wishlists 😊)



xoxo Smashlore & Taky

notes.title: Update #001:🚆🦖Railborn
notes.notes:
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31320585/6c1f2baa52448890ec9a2c3006a165317fc9aba1.jpg"]

Hi all! Welcome to our first Update for Railborn! 🎉🎉 If you’re new to the Washbear family – our first game was Parkasaurus. 🦖

 

Railborn has been in development for 2 years now – and we are very excited (relieved?) to finally be able to share what we’ve been working on. Just like with Parkasaurus, we plan to develop Railborn alongside our community, taking feedback and ideas.💡 I know, I know, a lot of developers say that - but we actually mean it. We've proved this with our development of Parkasaurus. Ask any of our community. 



Our community was the rock solid foundation 🪨 that helped make Parkasaurus a success, and with your help we hope to do it again with Railborn🤘. 



[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31320585/72dd631b7ddb4eb3b85540b91e9655728506b5df.gif"]



The first HUGE favor you can do for us (yes, you will hear me drone on about this a LOT 🙄) is to:


Wishlist Railborn and pass on the link to your friends!


Why? Well – Wishlists are really important to let Steam know people are interested in the game, and also let us make the game bigger and better. So – more Wishlists, better awesomer game. (awesomer IS a word I swear).

 

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31320585/af9994d10f0d96ded73fb3877a4ea463e1ddfe6d.jpg"]

Please feel free to hang out with us in our Discord or follow us on our manyyy socials.



I like to update regularly with what’s new in development here – so expect a lot of random thoughts and screenshots of what we’re doing.

 

I’m happy you’re here with us and look forward to this adventure!

 

xoxo Smashlore & Taky
